meta.source: bench/p500/results/P500_REPORT_v2.md — 'Per-group results' median ns/op tables (VERBATIM, never tuned to make the gate pass)
meta.source_commit: 3baa0f7 (REAL 120ms-batch rerun that produced P500_REPORT_v2.md; report introduced in 514378b)
meta.methodology: P500_REPORT_v2 paired-ratio methodology: absolute ns/op on a shared 2-CPU box is noisy - treat <±15% deltas as parity; RATIOS are the signal. The gate therefore compares each measured kernel median to its OWN verbatim baseline median (paired, per-kernel) inside a group, never group-vs-group absolutes. Repeated measurements of a kernel collapse via min-of-medians, mirroring the aggregator v2 rule.
meta.gate: fail (exit 1) when any included kernel's measured median > 1.2 x its baseline median (same 20% drift band the v2 aggregator uses for baseline.tsv: BASELINE_DRIFT = 0.20). Missing groups / CRASHed groups / groups absent from baseline => skip-with-warning (the >3-CRASH gate in the p500-bench job handles crashes). The 1.2 threshold is hardcoded in bench/p500/scripts/ratio_gate.py - deliberately NOT configurable from this file, so it cannot be quietly weakened.
meta.selection_rationale: Smoke subset = 5 JNI-floor parity groups from the v2 report's 'JNI floor groups' table: fastest groups in the suite (seconds per JVM), per-op cost dominated by the fixed JNI-transition floor (least hardware-dependent signal), exact old/alt 1:1 pairs with no multi-pair warnings, and all in the v2 PARITY band (no known wins/regressions that would trip the gate on every run). Regressed do-not-wire kernels (LevelChunkHeightmap, MarkerCache, PalettedReencodeScratch, ProtoChunkHeightmap) are deliberately excluded: they are known-bad alt kernels, not .so regressions.
